elicitation_input.question: Held during the Boer War, what nickname was given to the UK General Election of 1900?

llm_generation.text:
The UK General Election of 1900 is commonly known as the **"Khaki Election"**.

This nickname reflects the fact that the election was held while the Second Boer War was ongoing, and the ruling Conservative government (led by the Marquess of Salisbury) called the election to capitalize on a wave of patriotic sentiment following British military successes in South Africa. The term "khaki" refers to the colour of the British Army uniforms worn during the conflict, symbolizing how the war dominated the political atmosphere and campaign rhetoric of the time. The Conservatives, campaigning heavily on patriotic and imperial themes, won a substantial victory.
